title: The Ghost of Marseille's old port
premise: August Zhou, a crash investigator haunted by the deaths of his wife and daughter in row twelve of Flight 4471, is approached by a stranger named Camille who claims he once saved her life—a favor he has no memory of. She demands repayment in the form of a sealed report he quietly kept from the official investigation: proof that the crash was caused by a sabotaged component sold by the powerful Delacroix shipping dynasty. As August digs deeper with Camille, an investigative journalist with her own debts to Marseille's underworld, they uncover that the sabotage was meant to kill a whistleblower aboard—and that the dynasty's heir will burn the city down to bury it. Hunted through the old port's alleys and betrayed by the one colleague August trusted, August must choose between handing over the report to save Camille's life or releasing it publicly and avenging his family at the cost of everything else. In the end, August broadcasts the truth from the port authority tower as Delacroix's men close in, survives by surrendering to the crowd of dockworkers who shield him, and finds that justice outside the law costs him his career but returns to him something like sleep.
about_author: Noor Reyes is a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent a decade reconstructing accidents no one wanted explained before turning to fiction. She writes from a narrow apartment above a fish market, where the smell of salt and diesel keeps her honest.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: August Zhou's POV. Two years after the crash, August works nights reconstructing other people's disasters and sleeps in ninety-minute fragments. A routine inspection of wreckage evidence triggers a full flashback to identifying his family's bodies. Emotional beat: grief calcified into ritual; establish his precision as both gift and wound.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: August's POV. A woman named Camille intercepts him outside the port authority, insisting he pulled her from a burning car on the Corniche—something August knows he never did. She leaves a brass token and a phone number. He checks records: the accident happened, but the rescuer was never identified. Beat: unease; the world tilts off its known axis.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Camille reveals she works for a fixer who collects debts on behalf of clients who prefer anonymity, and the 'favor' was engineered to create leverage. What she actually wants: the sealed metallurgical annex from the Flight 4471 file, which August copied before it vanished. Beat: dread mixed with a dangerous flicker of hope—someone finally believes him.

chapters.title: The Annex
chapters.summary: August's POV. August retrieves the hidden copy from a locker at Saint-Charles station and rereads what he found two years ago: stress fractures consistent with a deliberately weakened actuator pin, sold through a shell company traced—barely—to Delacroix Maritime. Beat: rage resurfacing; the secret stops being a burden and becomes a weapon.

chapters.title: A Client Who Prefers Shadows
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Camille reports to her handler, Vasseur, and realizes the client demanding the annex isn't seeking justice—they want it destroyed. She conceals this from August. Flashback to how Vasseur owns her: a brother in prison, a debt of silence. Beat: complicity; love and duty begin their collision.

chapters.title: Dockside Conversations
chapters.summary: August's POV. August follows the shell company's paper trail to a retired crane operator, Baptiste, who saw crates moved the night before the crash and mentions 'the young Delacroix' watching from a black sedan. That night someone searches August's apartment. Beat: paranoia tightening; the investigation acquires witnesses and enemies simultaneously.

chapters.title: What Camille Wants
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Over pastis at a bar near the old port, August and Camille trade truths—her brother, his row twelve—and an unspoken alliance becomes something warmer. She admits she no longer knows whose side she's on. Beat: tenderness against duty; the first moment either has felt human in years.

chapters.title: The Heir
chapters.summary: Antoine Delacroix's POV. Introduce the antagonist: Antoine, polished and hollow, who ordered the sabotage to kill auditor Émile Roche aboard Flight 4471 and has since bought judges, journalists, and the port police chief. He learns the annex exists. Beat: cold menace; power shown as addiction.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes of Sleep
chapters.summary: August's POV. For the first time since the crash, August sleeps through the night—in Camille's apartment. He wakes believing he's been given a second life, then finds photographs of Camille slipped under his door: pictures of them together, taken days ago. Beat: fragile peace shattered; intimacy weaponized.

chapters.title: Vasseur's Ledger
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Camille confronts Vasseur, who admits the client is Delacroix and offers her a way out: deliver August and the annex, and her brother walks free. She asks for three days. Beat: impossible arithmetic—her brother's life priced against the man she's falling for.

chapters.title: Baptiste's Silence
chapters.summary: August's POV. August returns to Baptiste's barge and finds it burned, the old man hospitalized and refusing to speak. In the ashes: another brass token, identical to Camille's. August understands the favor network reaches everywhere. Beat: guilt and fury; every step forward costs someone else.

chapters.title: The Colleague
chapters.summary: August's POV. August turns to his trusted colleague Inspector Lefèvre for protection, showing him the annex. Lefèvre promises to run the serial numbers quietly. Unbeknownst to August, Lefèvre makes a call within the hour. Beat: dramatic irony; the reader sees the trap closing before August does.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Camille copies the annex and prepares to hand it over, then discovers Vasseur plans to have August killed regardless—the client wants no loose ends, including hers. She burns her copy and warns August. Beat: betrayal averted at the last breath; love chooses itself over duty.

chapters.title: Runners on the Corniche
chapters.summary: August and Camille dual POV. The pair goes on the run along the coast road, dodging port police using official channels to track them. A chase through the Vallon des Auffes ends with Camille shot in the shoulder; August carries her to a smuggler who owes the dead a debt. Beat: desperation; the law fully revealed as the enemy.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Price
chapters.summary: New POV: Marius, the smuggler. Marius shelters them in a sea cave and reveals his own history—his son died on Flight 4471, seat eleven. He agrees to help broadcast the annex if August can reach the port authority's legacy transmitter. Beat: grief finding fellowship; the crew of the wronged assembles.

chapters.title: Lefèvre's Confession
chapters.summary: Lefèvre's POV. Cornered by Antoine's fixers, Lefèvre realizes he's next on the list once August is dead. He defects, delivering the port authority access codes and a confession recorded for insurance. Beat: redemption purchased too late to be clean; corruption devours its own.

chapters.title: What the Annex Is Worth
chapters.summary: Antoine's POV. Antoine offers August everything—money, reinstatement, a name cleared—if he surrenders the annex, framing it as mercy. August hears his wife's voice in his memory asking what justice means if it's for sale. He refuses. Beat: the theme crystallized; power cannot comprehend refusal.

chapters.title: The Tower
chapters.summary: August's POV. Climax begins: August infiltrates the port authority tower during a storm while Camille and Marius hold the ground floor against Delacroix's men. Lefèvre's codes work until they don't. Beat: breathless ascent; every chapter's tension funnels into one room.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: August's POV. Wounded, August transmits the annex to every newsroom, regulator, and dockworker frequency in the Mediterranean as Antoine's men breach the tower. He reads his family's names into the open air before the signal cuts. Beat: catharsis; the secret worth killing for becomes a public inheritance.

chapters.title: The Crowd at the Water
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Antoine orders August's execution on the quay, but hundreds of dockworkers, summoned by the broadcast, stand between guns and investigator. Antoine's own security refuses the order; he's arrested as federal investigators arrive holding Lefèvre's confession. Beat: justice outside the law completed by the people inside it.

chapters.title: Interest Paid
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Aftermath: Vasseur arrested, Camille's brother freed, her debt dissolved not by payment but by testimony. She and August stand at the crash memorial, where row twelve's names are newly legible beneath fresh rain. Beat: mourning allowed at last; love that survived duty.

chapters.title: Through the Night
chapters.summary: August's POV. Months later, August testifies at the tribunal, declines his old job, and takes work teaching crash reconstruction to students who ask hard questions. On the final page, he sleeps until morning and wakes to sunlight and Camille making coffee. Beat: resolution; the ghost of the old port finally rests.
